body: The snapshot's text bounds and text extents are now measured from the bundled font set on every run path; the snapshot text form's parts and node bounds must read the same on every CI OS.
The accessibility tree's node bounds, which the snapshot reads, follow text shaped from the bundled set rather than the host's fonts.
The lint's contrast finding (its bounds, its ratio, its required value) is one of the readings compared across OSes; it must read the same from the bundled set.

Open select list rows (one row height, an open list's row bounds, a closed select's option bounds, a multiple select's row bounds) are laid out from text the bundled set shapes, and must read the same across OSes.
Hidpi or zoom changes reshape text: the reshaped text must still come from the bundled set, never fall back to host fonts.

The stand's checks that read text from the shaped page (the stand reads no lint finding at boot, SC 1.4.3 contrast asserted and measured from computed styles) must keep holding with the bundled set on every run path.
The driver's screenshot: no shot is compared by bytes across OSes; a screenshot still changes nothing and an element or row shot is unchanged in what it answers.

The driver's refusal causes gain nothing: fonts-unavailable stays the refusal for an app with no paintable font family, its text unchanged, and no new cause, field, verb, argument or carrier is added.
The snapshot model stays the single source the readers share; the cross-OS comparison reads the snapshot and the lint's findings through that model, adding no new reading.
The obs log format gains no field and no span: no new log field or span is added by the bundling.
Text runs label their parent element and the open list's option labels leave only as pixels: the text those readings take is shaped from the bundled set, their meaning unchanged.
No change to which font a remote page or the browser app reads, unless it is brought to the founder as an engine-change fork.

Where the bundled set is held: in the document's font context (the document configuration a document is built from), reachable by a later canvas painter, not a stand-local constant alone; canvas text is named as a future reader of it.

Generic family resolution: sans-serif, serif, monospace and an unknown family resolve to the bundled set, under the default-font fallback when no listed family is available and the rule that no generic family means sans-serif.

No change to which font a remote page or the browser app reads; any change there is an engine behaviour change that goes to the founder as a fork, flagged as a direct engine change.

Readings carry no process-local values: the snapshot and its text form read the same across hosts, with text extents and bounds the only geometry compared.

body: The font context of every run path — stand boot, driver session served tasks, shared fixture pages, and a harness-built document naming no font context — holds the bundled DejaVu Sans with system fonts off.
Harness construction: a document built through the harness with no font context of its own reaches the bundled set, not the host's system collection.
Generic family resolution: sans-serif, serif, monospace and an unknown family each resolve to the bundled font, never a host font.

fonts-unavailable kept: the driver refusal cause and the harness screenshot refusal still refuse an app whose font context holds no paintable family, before anything is painted or read, with its text unchanged.

No shot compared by bytes across OSes: the cross-OS proof compares readings only and holds no screenshot step.
Stand checks run under the bundled pinned real font and never skip for a missing font; font-metric tests never skip.
Font-dependent assertions no longer read the host's system fonts on a run path; any existing rule that such assertions rely on system fonts is reached by this change.
The native platform CI matrix: the test leg's Linux, macOS and Windows runners are where the cross-OS reading is held.
Stand checks are run in both layout modes and repeated in the stand-repeat rounds under a zero-failure budget; the bundled-font change must stay inside both.
Shared fixture pages, stated once, boot under the bundled font context; the stand boots offline from an asset already in the tree.

Recorded checks replayed as tests and kept byte-equal to the binary's recording: a reading the bundled font changes (text extents, bounds) means the committed recordings are re-recorded and stay fresh.
Boundary on the surface: no new carrier, verb, argument, field, refusal cause, log field or span; the refusal cause set and its printed form stay as they are.

Boundary on the engine: no change to which font a remote page or the browser app reads, unless brought to the founder as an engine-change fork; a fork goes to the run's founder-forks file and a deferral to the 0.4.0 deferred list.
No new dependency crate; the bundled font is a file already in the tree.

Canvas text left open: the bundled set is reachable through the document's font context for a later GlyphRun painter, and the acceptance names canvas text as a future reader; handler coverage's canvas limits are untouched.
